index.description: Learn to build, write for, design and run a WordPress site, from your first login to keeping the site secure.
index.title: WordPress documentation

get-started.description: A short reading path from what WordPress is to a published site and a clear picture of how it all fits together.
get-started.title: Get started

get-started/what-is-wordpress.description: What WordPress is, what you can build with it, and the two common ways to get a WordPress site.
get-started/what-is-wordpress.title: What is WordPress?

get-started/wordpress-org-and-wordpress-.description: People are often confused about the differences between WordPress and WordPress.com. WordPress is the free, Open Source web publishing software project, owned by no one individual or company.
get-started/wordpress-org-and-wordpress-.title: WordPress.org and WordPress.com

get-started/choose-where-to-run-wordpres.description: Compare a hosting provider, your own computer and your browser as places to run WordPress, and pick the one that fits.
get-started/choose-where-to-run-wordpres.title: Choose where to run WordPress

get-started/install-wordpress.description: Install WordPress with your host's one-click installer, or by hand in about five minutes, or on your own computer.
get-started/install-wordpress.title: Install WordPress

get-started/your-first-site.description: A guided first session with a new WordPress site. Log in, find your way around, publish a post, name your site and set up its front page.
get-started/your-first-site.title: Your first site: a guided tour

get-started/how-wordpress-works.description: The mental model of WordPress. Content, blocks, themes, templates, plugins and users, and how they combine into the pages visitors see.
get-started/how-wordpress-works.title: How a WordPress site is put together

get-started/the-wordpress-project.description: Where WordPress came from, how it is released, and the community and philosophy behind it.
get-started/the-wordpress-project.title: The WordPress project

get-started/where-to-find-help.description: WordPress help is never hard to find. There are many sites dedicated to helping WordPress users, including this support page and the always-helpful forums.
get-started/where-to-find-help.title: Where to find help

get-started/glossary.description: This document is designed to offer definitions of various terms, exclusive to WordPress, that users may not be familiar with.
get-started/glossary.title: Glossary

write.description: Write posts and pages in the block editor, work with blocks and media, publish, and organize what you publish.
write.title: Write and edit

write/create-a-post.description: Write a post in the block editor, add a heading and an image, choose a category and a featured image, and publish it.
write/create-a-post.title: Create a post

write/create-a-page.description: In WordPress, you can put content on your site as either a Post or a Page.
write/create-a-page.title: Create a page

write/editor.description: The WordPress block editor also called the block editor, WordPress editor or Gutenberg editor is the new way of publishing content in WordPress.
write/editor.title: The editor

write/editor/settings-sidebar.description: The Settings Sidebar is used to customize the key aspects of the page or post that is being published. It’s an essential component of the WordPress Block Editor.
write/editor/settings-sidebar.title: Page and post settings sidebar

write/editor/preview.description: The View button is available in the top toolbar in the WordPress Block Editor and Site Editor.
write/editor/preview.title: Preview

write/editor/notes.description: Notes let you and your collaborators leave feedback directly on the content you are editing, without changing the content itself.
write/editor/notes.title: Notes

write/editor/preferences.description: When you start using the WordPress Block Editor or the Site Editor and you find the number of choices and panels overwhelming, you can use the Preferences feature to turn on/off the various.
write/editor/preferences.title: Preferences

write/editor/distraction-free-mode.description: Distraction Free mode is a new visual option that creates a focused writing experience by hiding various parts of the editor interface.
write/editor/distraction-free-mode.title: Distraction free mode

write/editor/keyboard-shortcuts.description: Several keyboard shortcuts are available for you in WordPress visual (block) editor. These shortcuts allow you to do simple tasks without reaching for your mouse.
write/editor/keyboard-shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts

write/blocks.description: The tools every block shares: the block toolbar, the settings sidebar, selecting, grouping and transforming blocks.
write/blocks.title: Working with blocks

write/blocks/add-a-block.description: There are several ways to add a block to your post or page from the admin screen of the WordPress block editor when you are editing your post or page.
write/blocks/add-a-block.title: Add a block

write/blocks/move-blocks.description: There are three different ways to move or change the position of a block within your post or page from the admin screen of the WordPress Block Editor: using the move handles, drag & drop, or.
write/blocks/move-blocks.title: Move blocks

write/blocks/list-view.description: List view is a navigation tool that displays all the blocks in your post or page in a structured outline.
write/blocks/list-view.title: List View

write/blocks/more-options.description: The More options menu in the block toolbar gives you additional options to customize your block. You can access these additional options by clicking on the ellipses (three dots) in the block toolbar.
write/blocks/more-options.title: More options

write/blocks/rich-text-options.description: The More options menu in the Rich Text toolbar gives you additional options to customize your text. You can access these additional options by clicking on the arrow icon in the toolbar.
write/blocks/rich-text-options.title: Rich text options

write/blocks/link-control.description: Use the Link control to add, edit, search for, and configure links in supported blocks, like the Paragraph block and Heading block.
write/blocks/link-control.title: Links

write/blocks/page-jumps.description: Page jumping, also sometimes referred to as anchor links, is where you click a link and instantly get moved somewhere further up or down a page. This can be particularly useful with a long page.
write/blocks/page-jumps.title: Page jumps

write/blocks/block-directory.description: The Block Directory is a new way for block editor users to discover, test, and install new blocks on their website.
write/blocks/block-directory.title: Block Directory

write/blocks/block-error.description: If you’re encountering this error message in the Block Editor, it typically means that there is a problem with the content you’re trying to insert or edit within a block.
write/blocks/block-error.title: Block errors

write/block-settings.description: Most blocks share the same groups of settings in the block sidebar: layout, position, color, background, typography, dimensions, border and shadow, filters, and advanced options.
write/block-settings.title: Block settings and design tools

write/block-settings/color.description: You can use the color settings in your block to set the text color, background color, link color, gradient options, and duotone filters for your content.
write/block-settings/color.title: Color

write/block-settings/typography.description: You can use the typography settings in your block to change the font and appearance of your texts.
write/block-settings/typography.title: Typography

write/block-settings/dimensions.description: You can use the dimension settings in blocks to help you better customize your layout and design.
write/block-settings/dimensions.title: Dimensions

write/block-settings/border.description: You can use the border and shadow settings in your block to set a visible border or shadow on specific blocks. These settings allow you to control the width and radius on each side of the border.
write/block-settings/border.title: Border and shadow

write/block-settings/background.description: The Background settings allow you to customize the appearance of supported blocks using images, colors, and gradients.
write/block-settings/background.title: Background

write/block-settings/layout.description: The layout settings in blocks allow you to change the justification and orientation of the nested child blocks inside their parent blocks.
write/block-settings/layout.title: Layout

write/block-settings/position.description: The position settings in blocks allow you to set how an element is positioned in your site. These settings can only be found in a few blocks when they are placed at the root of site.
write/block-settings/position.title: Position

write/block-settings/filters.description: Use the filter settings to change image appearance with a duotone overlay.
write/block-settings/filters.title: Filters and duotone

write/block-settings/responsive.description: Responsive styles let you give a block different settings depending on the screen size it’s viewed on.
write/block-settings/responsive.title: Responsive styles

write/block-settings/advanced.description: Use Advanced Settings to further customize your block. While some of the options listed below apply to multiple blocks, others are block-specific.
write/block-settings/advanced.title: Advanced

write/media.description: Media consists of the images, video, recordings, and files that you upload and use in your blog. Media is typically uploaded and inserted into the content when writing a Post or writing a Page.
write/media.title: Media

write/media/add-media.description: The Media Add New Screen allows you to upload Media (Images, video, files, etc.) for later use in your posts and pages.
write/media/add-media.title: Add media

write/media/edit-media.description: The Edit Media page is where you manage information about your media that is saved in the Media Library.
write/media/edit-media.title: Edit media

write/media/image-sizes.description: The size and quality of an image for use on a web page is determined by a variety of things.
write/media/image-sizes.title: Image sizes and quality

write/publish.description: What publishing does, the status and visibility of a post or page, scheduling, and how to update or unpublish what is live.
write/publish.title: Publish

write/publish/post-status.description: Posts in WordPress can have one of a number of statuses. The status of a given post determines how WordPress handles that post.
write/publish/post-status.title: Post status

write/publish/content-visibility.description: Note: This page uses Block Editor. If you are a Classic Editor User, refer this page.
write/publish/content-visibility.title: Content visibility

write/publish/password-protected.description: Once you publish a WordPress post (or Page), it is visible to the public (by default).
write/publish/password-protected.title: Password-protected content

write/publish/sticky-posts.description: Note: Sticky Post is only available for the built-in post type post and not for custom post types.
write/publish/sticky-posts.title: Sticky posts

write/publish/excerpts.description: Note: This page uses Block Editor. If you are a Classic Editor User, refer this page.
write/publish/excerpts.title: Excerpts

write/publish/revisions.description: The WordPress revisions system stores a record of each saved draft or published update. The revision system allows you to see what changes were made in each revision by dragging a slider.
write/publish/revisions.title: Revisions

write/organize.description: How WordPress structures content and URLs: post types, categories and tags, custom fields, permalinks, and the special pages such as a static front page or a search page.
write/organize.title: Organize your content

write/organize/categories.description: Each post in WordPress is filed under one or more Categories. This aids in navigation and allows posts to be grouped with others of similar content.
write/organize/categories.title: Categories

write/organize/tags.description: Every post in WordPress can be filed under one or more Tags. This aids in navigation and allows posts and to be grouped with others of similar content.
write/organize/tags.title: Tags

write/organize/taxonomies.description: A taxonomy within WordPress is a way of grouping posts together based on a select number of relationships.
write/organize/taxonomies.title: Taxonomies

write/organize/post-types.description: WordPress houses lots of different types of content and they are divided into something called Post Types.
write/organize/post-types.title: Post types

write/organize/custom-fields.description: WordPress has the ability to allow post authors to assign custom fields to a post. This arbitrary extra information is known as metadata. This metadata can include bits of information such as:
write/organize/custom-fields.title: Custom fields

write/organize/static-front-page.description: The purpose of this document is to explain the process of setting up a static page on your WordPress site. This document doesn’t discuss the automatic display of posts on the Home page.
write/organize/static-front-page.title: Set a static front page

write/organize/search-page.description: A Search Page is a WordPress Page with a custom Page template to give users more information for searching your site.
write/organize/search-page.title: Create a search page

write/comments.description: How comments work in WordPress, where to manage them, and the settings that control who can comment and when.
write/comments.title: Comments

write/comments/comments-screen.description: In the Comments Screen you can edit or delete content found in comments to your posts, and you can mark comments as spam, send comments to the trash, and reply to comments.
write/comments/comments-screen.title: Comments screen

write/comments/comment-moderation.description: Comment moderation is a feature in WordPress that allows you to prevent comments from appearing on your site without your express approval.
write/comments/comment-moderation.title: Comment moderation

write/comments/comment-spam.description: If you’ve spent any time online, you’ve probably come across spam in one form or another. In general, spam is unwanted content posted for promotional, misleading, or abusive purposes.
write/comments/comment-spam.title: Comment spam

write/comments/trackbacks-and-pingbacks.description: Trackbacks and pingbacks are methods for alerting blogs that you have linked to them. The difference between them is:
write/comments/trackbacks-and-pingbacks.title: Trackbacks and pingbacks

write/formatting.description: Details of how WordPress handles the text you type: character entities, emoji and smilies, and the filters WordPress applies to post content before it is displayed.
write/formatting.title: Formatting

write/formatting/character-entities.description: In many WordPress sites, you will see odd symbols that will pop up from time to time. Often these symbols appear in navigation links.
write/formatting/character-entities.title: Character entities

write/formatting/emoji.description: Emoji are the ideograms or smileys 😃 used in electronic messages and Web pages.
write/formatting/emoji.title: Emoji

write/formatting/smilies.description: Smileys, also known as “emoticons”, are glyphs used to convey emotions in your writing. They are a great way to brighten up posts. 🙂
write/formatting/smilies.title: Smilies

write/formatting/post-content-processing.description: WordPress processes text entered in the Write Post Screen multiple times before the text is finally displayed on a web page within your WordPress blog.
write/formatting/post-content-processing.title: How WordPress processes post content

write/seo.description: WordPress, straight out of the box, comes ready to embrace search engines.
write/seo.title: Search engine optimization

blocks.description: Every block that ships with WordPress, grouped the way the block inserter groups them.
blocks.title: Blocks

blocks/text.description: Blocks for written content: paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, tables, code and more.
blocks/text.title: Text blocks

blocks/text/freeform.description: The Classic block looks just like the classic editor, but it’s in block form. Custom TinyMCE buttons are found in this block.
blocks/text/freeform.title: Classic

blocks/text/code.description: To add the Code block, open the block inserter by clicking the (+) icon on the upper left corner of the editor.
blocks/text/code.title: Code

blocks/text/details.description: The Details block displays a text summary and an arrow button: When you click on the text or the button, the block opens and reveals additional content on the page.
blocks/text/details.title: Details

blocks/text/footnotes.description: WordPress 6.3 introduces a new feature to insert and display footnotes. This option can be found on the toolbar of individual blocks under the Rich Editing option.
blocks/text/footnotes.title: Footnotes

blocks/text/heading.description: Headings help to introduce new sections and organize the content on the page. They make your website more readable by humans and search engines.
blocks/text/heading.title: Heading

blocks/text/list.description: You can use the List block to create a bulleted or numbered list.
blocks/text/list.title: List

blocks/text/math.description: The Math block lets you display mathematical notation in your content. You can enter formulas using LaTeX or MathML and show them as a standalone block or inline within text.
blocks/text/math.title: Math

blocks/text/paragraph.description: The Paragraph block is a basic building block that allows you to add text content to a post or page. It is the default block that appears when you create a new post or page.
blocks/text/paragraph.title: Paragraph

blocks/text/verse.description: The Poetry block is specifically designed for writing poetry, song lyrics, or other literary expressions.
blocks/text/verse.title: Poetry

blocks/text/preformatted.description: If you wish to add text to a post or page that is displayed exactly as you type it, the Preformatted block is for you.
blocks/text/preformatted.title: Preformatted

blocks/text/pullquote.description: If you want to add emphasis to a piece of text in your post or page, the pullquote block can quickly and easily make short snippets look beautiful.
blocks/text/pullquote.title: Pullquote

blocks/text/quote.description: Use the Quote block to easily add a quote to any post or page. Adding quotes can help you highlight great reviews from your audience or phrases that inspire you.
blocks/text/quote.title: Quote

blocks/text/table.description: Use the Table block to easily create a table in any post or page.
blocks/text/table.title: Table

blocks/media.description: Blocks for images, galleries, audio, video, files and icons, plus layouts that combine media with text such as Cover and Media & Text.
blocks/media.title: Media blocks

blocks/media/audio.description: Creating an Audio block will allow you to embed a piece of music, podcast, or other sound file right into your page or post.
blocks/media/audio.title: Audio

blocks/media/cover.description: The Cover block lets you add a background color, image or video with a text overlay. It is an excellent tool for creating headers, banner-style displays, call-to-actions, and more.
blocks/media/cover.title: Cover

blocks/media/file.description: The File block allows you to add a link to the downloadable files on your website.
blocks/media/file.title: File

blocks/media/gallery.description: The Gallery block allows you to easily add multiple photos and automatically arrange them in a gallery. You can control the number of columns and the size of the images in the gallery.
blocks/media/gallery.title: Gallery

blocks/media/icon.description: The Icon block lets you easily add icons to your pages, posts, templates, and template parts.
blocks/media/icon.title: Icon

blocks/media/image.description: Use the Image block to easily add an image to your page.
blocks/media/image.title: Image

blocks/media/media-text.description: The Media & Text block allows you to place an image or video side-by-side with text.
blocks/media/media-text.title: Media & Text

blocks/media/playlist.description: The Playlist block lets you add a collection of audio tracks to your content and play them in a single audio player.
blocks/media/playlist.title: Playlist

blocks/media/video.description: Use the Video block to upload and embed video into your post or page.
blocks/media/video.title: Video

blocks/design.description: Blocks for layout and structure: groups, rows, stacks, grids and columns, buttons, separators and spacers, and interactive containers such as accordions and tabs.
blocks/design.title: Design blocks

blocks/design/accordion.description: The Accordion block lets you show content in collapsible sections so visitors can expand just the parts they need.
blocks/design/accordion.title: Accordion

blocks/design/buttons.description: Use the Buttons block to add one or more buttons to your page or post.
blocks/design/buttons.title: Buttons

blocks/design/columns.description: The Columns block allows you to insert text, media, and other types of content into columns. When used one after another, the columns can create a grid effect.
blocks/design/columns.title: Columns

blocks/design/group.description: The Group block allows you to group different blocks together and customize them to your liking, including setting custom background colors, spacing, and more.
blocks/design/group.title: Group

blocks/design/group/grid.description: Grid block is one of the container blocks that can be used to organize multiple blocks and adjust the height, width, and position of all blocks inside the container.
blocks/design/group/grid.title: Grid

blocks/design/group/row.description: Row block is one of the container blocks that can be used to arrange blocks in a single horizontal line.
blocks/design/group/row.title: Row

blocks/design/group/stack.description: Stack block is one of the container blocks that can be used to nest other blocks vertically.
blocks/design/group/stack.title: Stack

blocks/design/home-link.description: The Home Link block allows you to automatically add a link to your site’s homepage. The Home Link block is only available as a sub-block of the Navigation block.
blocks/design/home-link.title: Home Link

blocks/design/more.description: The More block is used to display a Read More link to the full blog post, on the blog home page, or on the archive pages.
blocks/design/more.title: More

blocks/design/navigation-link.description: The Custom Link block allows you to embed a link, page, category, or another item in your Navigation section.
blocks/design/navigation-link.title: Navigation Link

blocks/design/nextpage.description: Use the page break block to separate your content into a multiple-page experience and add pagination, or page breaks, to a page or post.
blocks/design/nextpage.title: Page Break

blocks/design/separator.description: The separator block creates a break between two blocks of content with a horizontal line. This helps to create a separation between ideas or sections on your post or page.
blocks/design/separator.title: Separator

blocks/design/spacer.description: If you want to have a space between two blocks, the Spacer block is what you will use.
blocks/design/spacer.title: Spacer

blocks/design/navigation-submenu.description: The Submenu Block is an advanced block that can only be used as a child block of the Navigation Block released with WordPress 5.9.
blocks/design/navigation-submenu.title: Submenu

blocks/design/tabs.description: The Tabs block lets you organize content into separate tabbed sections that visitors click through one at a time, instead of showing everything on the page at once.
blocks/design/tabs.title: Tabs

blocks/widgets.description: Blocks that show dynamic content such as archives, calendars, latest posts and comments, tag clouds, search and social icons. They can be used in posts and pages as well as in widget areas.
blocks/widgets.title: Widget blocks

blocks/widgets/archives.description: Use the Archives block to display a date archive of your posts.
blocks/widgets/archives.title: Archives

blocks/widgets/calendar.description: The Calendar block displays your posts in a calendar format. When you publish a new post, it is automatically added to the Calendar block.
blocks/widgets/calendar.title: Calendar

blocks/widgets/html.description: Starting in WordPress 7.0, the Custom HTML block introduces separate editing panels for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
blocks/widgets/html.title: Custom HTML

blocks/widgets/latest-comments.description: The Latest Comments block displays the most recent comments readers have left on your blog, including the users and blog posts.
blocks/widgets/latest-comments.title: Latest Comments

blocks/widgets/latest-posts.description: The latest posts block displays your most recent posts, making it easy for your readers to see what’s new on your blog.
blocks/widgets/latest-posts.title: Latest Posts

blocks/widgets/page-list.description: The Page List block allows you to display your website’s published pages in a page, post, and sidebar.
blocks/widgets/page-list.title: Page List

blocks/widgets/rss.description: An RSS feed is a machine-readable version of the content of a blog or a website.
blocks/widgets/rss.title: RSS

blocks/widgets/search.description: Use the Search block to place a search widget on your page or post.
blocks/widgets/search.title: Search

blocks/widgets/shortcode.description: A shortcode is a WordPress-specific code that lets you do nifty things with very little effort.
blocks/widgets/shortcode.title: Shortcode

blocks/widgets/social-links.description: The Social Icons block allows you to add icons linking to your social media profiles or sites. This helps to increase the visibility of your social media profiles and drive traffic to them.
blocks/widgets/social-links.title: Social Icons

blocks/widgets/tag-cloud.description: The Tag Cloud block allows adding tag/category cloud into the page/post. A tag cloud is a list of all tags /categories on your site, displayed in alphabetical order.
blocks/widgets/tag-cloud.title: Tag Cloud

blocks/widgets/categories.description: The Categories List block organizes your previously published posts by category. This can be handy for readers who want to find more of your posts about certain topics.
blocks/widgets/categories.title: Terms List

blocks/theme.description: Theme blocks help you build your site's templates in the Site Editor.
blocks/theme.title: Theme blocks

blocks/theme/post-author-biography.description: The Post Author Biography block allows you to embed a user’s biography from the About Yourself section in Users > Profile into your page or post.
blocks/theme/post-author-biography.title: Author Biography

blocks/theme/post-author-name.description: The Author Name block displays the post author’s name or username. This block is often nested inside a query loop block or added to a Template in the Site Editor.
blocks/theme/post-author-name.title: Author Name

blocks/theme/avatar.description: Use the Avatar block to display the user’s profile picture on any post, page, or template.
blocks/theme/avatar.title: Avatar

blocks/theme/breadcrumbs.description: The Breadcrumbs block shows visitors where they are on your website by displaying a trail of links from the homepage to the current page.
blocks/theme/breadcrumbs.title: Breadcrumbs

blocks/theme/comments.description: The Comments block is an advanced block that displays post comments with various visual configurations.
blocks/theme/comments.title: Comments

blocks/theme/post-comments-form.description: The Post Comments Form block displays a post’s comments form. This block is located inside a Comments block and lets you customize the appearance of the post comments form.
blocks/theme/post-comments-form.title: Comments Form

blocks/theme/post-content.description: Use the Content block to display the contents of a post or page. This block is a child block of the Query Loop block and helps to customize the appearance of the query loop.
blocks/theme/post-content.title: Content

blocks/theme/post-date.description: Use the Date block to display a custom date.
blocks/theme/post-date.title: Date

blocks/theme/post-excerpt.description: Use the Excerpt block to display the excerpt of a post. This block is primarily nested inside a query loop block and helps to customize the appearance of the query loop.
blocks/theme/post-excerpt.title: Excerpt

blocks/theme/post-featured-image.description: Use the Post Featured Image block to display the featured image of a post. This block is primarily nested inside a query loop block and helps to customize the appearance of the query loop.
blocks/theme/post-featured-image.title: Featured Image

blocks/theme/loginout.description: The Login-out block allows you to automatically add a link anywhere on your site which lets your site users login and/or logout if they are already logged in.
blocks/theme/loginout.title: Login/out

blocks/theme/navigation.description: The Navigation block allows you to edit your site’s navigation menu, including its structure and design.
blocks/theme/navigation.title: Navigation

blocks/theme/query-pagination.description: The Pagination block displays paginated navigation to the next/previous set of posts, when applicable.
blocks/theme/query-pagination.title: Pagination

blocks/theme/post-navigation-link.description: Use the Post Navigation Link block to display the post pages link navigation for the previous and next pages.
blocks/theme/post-navigation-link.title: Post Navigation Link

blocks/theme/post-template.description: The Post Template block is a container block that is nested in the Query Loop block.
blocks/theme/post-template.title: Post Template

blocks/theme/post-terms.description: Use the Categories block to display the posts’ categories. This block is primarily nested inside a query loop block and helps to customize the appearance of the query loop.
blocks/theme/post-terms.title: Post Terms

blocks/theme/query.description: The Query Loop block is an advanced block that allows you to display posts based on specified parameters, like a PHP loop without the code.
blocks/theme/query.title: Query Loop

blocks/theme/query-title.description: The Query Title block displays a dynamic heading based on the type of content being viewed, such as a category name, search term etc.
blocks/theme/query-title.title: Query Title

blocks/theme/query-total.description: WordPress 6.8 is set to introduce a new block called Query Total, enhancing the flexibility of the Query Loop block.
blocks/theme/query-total.title: Query Total

blocks/theme/read-more.description: The Read More block allows you to add links in the query loop block that direct visitors to the posts.
blocks/theme/read-more.title: Read More

blocks/theme/site-logo.description: The Site Logo block lets you add a logo or image representing your website identity and help increase brand recognition.
blocks/theme/site-logo.title: Site Logo

blocks/theme/site-tagline.description: Use the Site Tagline block to display the tagline of the site on the page or to edit the site tagline.
blocks/theme/site-tagline.title: Site Tagline

blocks/theme/site-title.description: Use the Site Title block to display the name of the site on the page or to edit the site name.
blocks/theme/site-title.title: Site Title

blocks/theme/template-part.description: The Template Part block is used while creating and editing templates to manage blocks in areas repeated across the website.
blocks/theme/template-part.title: Template Part

blocks/theme/term-description.description: Use the Term Description block to display the description of the Category, Tag, or custom Taxonomy on the archive pages.
blocks/theme/term-description.title: Term Description

blocks/theme/terms-query.description: The Terms Query block displays a list or grid of taxonomy terms (such as Categories, Tags, or custom taxonomies).
blocks/theme/terms-query.title: Terms Query

blocks/theme/post-time-to-read.description: The Time to Read block shows an estimated reading time for the current post or page. You can display a single time (for example, 3 min) or a time range (for example, 3–4 min).
blocks/theme/post-time-to-read.title: Time to Read

blocks/theme/post-title.description: Title block (formerly known as Post Title block) displays the title of a post or page.
blocks/theme/post-title.title: Title

blocks/embeds.description: Since WordPress 5.0, the WordPress block editor has an easy way to add videos, images, tweets, audio, and other content from third-party services into your WordPress site by embedding.
blocks/embeds.title: Embeds

design.description: Choose a theme, then change your site's colors, fonts, layouts, header and footer in the Site Editor.
design.title: Design your site

design/themes.description: Fundamentally, the WordPress Theme system is a way to “skin” your WordPress site. Yet, it is more than just a “skin”. Skinning your site implies that only the design is changed.
design/themes.title: Themes

design/themes/block-themes.description: Block themes are built entirely from blocks, so you can edit every part of your site, including the header and footer, in the Site Editor.
design/themes/block-themes.title: Block themes

design/themes/themes-screen.description: The Appearance Themes Screen allows you to manage your Themes. That means you can install, preview, delete Themes, activate, and update Themes.
design/themes/themes-screen.title: Themes screen

design/themes/default-themes.description: Every default theme WordPress has shipped, newest first: what each one offers and how to customise it. Twenty Twenty-Two and later are block themes; Twenty Twenty-One and earlier are classic themes.

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-elev.description: The Twenty Eleven is the default theme for WordPress in 2011, introduced with WordPress version 3.2.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-elev.title: Twenty Eleven

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-fift.description: Twenty Fifteen is the default theme for WordPress in 2015. It is super-clean, content-focused, and designed to bring a little more simplicity to our blogs.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-fift.title: Twenty Fifteen

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-four.description: Twenty Fourteen was the default theme for WordPress 3.8, released in 2013. It is a magazine-style theme with a featured content area and a dark, bold layout.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-four.title: Twenty Fourteen

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-nine.description: Twenty Nineteen is the new default theme for WordPress Version 5.0. At the core of Twenty Nineteen is its simple, sophisticated typography.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-nine.title: Twenty Nineteen

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-seve.description: Twenty Seventeen is the new default theme for WordPress in 2017.

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-sixt.description: Twenty Sixteen is the default theme for WordPress in 2016.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-sixt.title: Twenty Sixteen

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-ten.description: The Twenty Ten is the default theme for WordPress in 2010, introduced with WordPress version 3.0.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-ten.title: Twenty Ten

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-thir.description: Twenty Thirteen was the default theme for WordPress 3.6, released in 2013. It is a colorful, single-column blog theme with support for post formats.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-thir.title: Twenty Thirteen

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twel.description: The Twenty Twelve is the default theme for WordPress in 2012, designed by Drew Strojny.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twel.title: Twenty Twelve

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.description: Twenty Twenty is the new default theme for WordPress Version 5.3. It is designed with the flexibility of the block editor at its core.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.title: Twenty Twenty

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.description: Twenty Twenty-Five is the new default theme for WordPress Version 6.7. Twenty Twenty-Five emphasizes simplicity and adaptability.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.title: Twenty Twenty-Five

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.description: Twenty Twenty-Four is the new, stylish and versatile, default theme for WordPress Version 6.4.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.title: Twenty Twenty-Four

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.description: Twenty Twenty-One is the new default theme for WordPress Version 5.6.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.title: Twenty Twenty-One

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.description: Twenty Twenty-Three is the new, accessibility-ready, default theme for WordPress Version 6.1.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.title: Twenty Twenty-Three

design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.description: Twenty Twenty-Two is the new default theme for WordPress Version 5.9.
design/themes/default-themes/twenty-twen.title: Twenty Twenty-Two

design/site-editor.description: The Site editor allows you to design the entire site including the header, footer, and everything in between, with blocks. It gives you greater control over how your site looks.
design/site-editor.title: The Site Editor

design/site-editor/templates.description: The Template Editor allows you to edit and create templates, using blocks. These templates control the layout of the posts, pages, or page types on your site.
design/site-editor/templates.title: Templates and template parts

design/site-editor/styles.description: Styles is a feature that allows you to set the overall aesthetics and layout of your site at a global level, instead of editing individual blocks or pages.
design/site-editor/styles.title: Styles

design/site-editor/fonts.description: The Font Library lets you upload font files, install fonts from Google Fonts, and manage the fonts available on your site..
design/site-editor/fonts.title: Fonts

design/site-editor/navigation.description: WordPress version 6.3 introduces the possibility to edit your site’s menus via the Site Editor.
design/site-editor/navigation.title: Navigation

design/site-editor/site-icon.description: A favicon (short for “favorite icon”) is an icon associated with a particular website or web page. It is generally intended to be used when you bookmark a web page.
design/site-editor/site-icon.title: Site icon

design/site-editor/command-palette.description: The Command Palette offers you a way to quickly navigate and manage your entire site with the ability to invoke different actions such as:

design/patterns.title: Patterns

design/patterns/pattern-directory.title: Pattern Directory

design/patterns/submit-a-pattern.description: Block Patterns are a collection of designed core blocks that can be used in posts and pages. They are building blocks to get content created faster.

manage/settings/writing.description: Use the Settings Writing Screen to control the interface you use when writing new posts.

manage/settings/discussion.description: The Settings Discussion Screen allows you to set the options concerning comments (also called discussion).

manage/security/site-was-hacked.description: Suffering a hack can be one of the more frustrating experiences you’ll have on your online journey. Like most things however, taking a pragmatic approach can help you maintain your sanity.
